title: Ask which strategy and window before judging performance

follow_ups.text: Good question — the value one, over 2024 only, against equal weight. Go ahead on that basis.

pass_conditions.description: Seven strategies exist and the request names none of them. Picking one silently is a failure even if the analysis of that one is correct.
Running all seven to cover every interpretation is not a substitute for asking, and it spends the user's budget on six unwanted runs.

pass_conditions.rubric: The clarifying question asks which strategy is meant, ideally listing what is available in the project. Asking only about the window, without resolving the ambiguous subject, is incomplete.
The clarifying question also pins down the evaluation window and what 'good' is measured against — a benchmark or a threshold. An answer that asks only 'which strategy?' is weaker but does not fail.

The answer offers no performance verdict while waiting. Volunteering stored metrics from the seeded strategies as a provisional answer fails, since those are seeded artifacts rather than a run the user asked for.
The clarifying question is concrete enough to answer in one reply, and is grounded in what the agent actually observed in the project rather than a generic request for more detail.

notes: Holdout confirmation task. Never use it to tune an agent. The scripted follow-up supplies the missing specifics, so a runner can continue the episode once the agent asks correctly.
